clinician.trajectory_summary: A 15-year-old male presented with fever, headache, projectile emesis, blurry vision, and involuntary movements for seven days. Initial examination revealed hypertension (BP 150/100 mmHg) and decreased visual acuity in the left eye. Laboratory investigations showed leukocytosis, positive IgM for Dengue, decreased complement 3, elevated anti-streptolysin (ASO) titers, uremia, hematuria, and proteinuria, supporting a diagnosis of post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis. Brain MRI revealed symmetrical enhancement in superficial and deep watershed areas, predominantly occipital and temporal, consistent with Posterior Reversible Encephalopathy Syndrome (PRES). The patient was treated with ceftriaxone and amlodipine. Six days post-admission, he was asymptomatic with minimal hematuria. A repeat MRI after three weeks showed complete resolution of the hyperintense lesions.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with neurological symptoms including headache, projectile emesis, blurry vision, and involuntary movements.
Initial blood pressure was significantly elevated at 150/100 mmHg (99th percentile), confirmed by 72-hour monitoring.
Neurological examination showed decreased visual acuity of the left eye.
Laboratory tests indicated kidney involvement and recent streptococcal infection: decreased complement 3, elevated anti-streptolysin (ASO) titers, uremia, hematuria, and proteinuria.
Brain MRI findings were remarkable for symmetrical enhancement of superficial and deep watershed areas, predominantly in the occipital and temporal regions, consistent with PRES.
Patient was treated with ceftriaxone and amlodipine, leading to clinical improvement.
Repeat MRI after three weeks showed complete resolution of hyperintense lesions, confirming the reversible nature of PRES.

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.alternative: Dengue fever as the primary cause of neurological/renal symptoms
ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: While positive IgM antibodies for Dengue were found (E003), the final diagnosis focused on PSGN and PRES, and the clinical trajectory and resolution were consistent with these diagnoses rather than Dengue being the sole or primary etiology for the severe neurological and renal manifestations.

remaining_uncertainties: Full resolution of all PSGN markers (proteinuria, uremia, C3, ASO titers) beyond 'minimal hematuria' at 6 days.
